text:
jordan: Quick PSA — running POC for ACME, we rotated keys this morning and now seeing intermittent 403s. Error in logs: "invalid_tenant_claim". Anyone seen this after rotation?

mike: @jordan can you paste the curl you used and the x-org header? request id would help too

jordan: sure
jordan: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc..." -H "X-Org: acme" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` 
jordan: logs show auth failure: 403 - invalid_tenant_claim (req=req-9f3a)

sarah: is this the prod key or a trial key for POC? if trial make sure org binding matches the tenant id we provisioned

jordan: trial sandbox key from the portal. the portal shows org_id = acme-int-2026. header was acme

mike: ah — mismatch. we bind keys to exact tenant id (acme-int-2026). two quick fixes: 1) update X-Org header to the tenant id, or 2) request a key for 'acme' env. 

infra-oncall: to confirm run this: ```curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc..." -H "X-Org: acme-int-2026" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health``` if 200 OK it's binding

jordan: running now...

jordan: got 200 OK. switching the POC to use the tenant id fixed the 403s. thanks!

sarah: great — looping in presales docs — we should add note in the onboarding checklist about tenant id vs friendly org header :memo:

presales-bot: Created ticket RED-3145 — Add tenant-id note to POC onboarding doc. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-3145 :white_check_mark:

mike: small follow-up: if customers rotate keys frequently, recommend using service-account tokens (project-scoped) and set up a short automation for rotation. happy to send an example

jordan: yes please send example, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
